liquidity_funding.text: The group repaid its interest-bearing financial liabilities in full, which the report says greatly reduces the sensitivity of the company to changes in interest rates.
A financing commitment was given to the City Air Terminal joint venture for new train sets, part of which was drawn as a loan in the year.
Free cash flow of {{fcf@FY2024}} remains the main internal source of funding, having fallen by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} as capital spending rose.
Undrawn committed facilities are not disclosed for the year, so the liquidity buffer rests on the cash generated and on the absence of interest-bearing financial liabilities.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, but traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} was well below the {{traffic_growth@FY2023}} of FY2023.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, supporting the revenue base as airport charges are temporarily adjusted by average inflation.

The investment programme, including the third runway against which complaints were filed over the extension of the construction completion deadline, is reflected in the capital spending discussed under credit metrics.

peer_positioning.text: Flughafen Wien has the lowest gross leverage of the airport group ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}), against a peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@FY2024}}.

On EBITDA margin the company sits in the middle of the group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), and it also sits in the middle of the group on capex intensity, at a peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}.
Traffic growth is the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}), below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@FY2024}}.

snapshot.text: Flughafen Wien, the Vienna airport group that also holds Malta and Košice airports, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, with the EBITDA margin broadly unchanged at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}.
Gross leverage stayed at {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} as total debt was broadly unchanged at {{total_debt@FY2024}}, and the group repaid its interest-bearing financial liabilities in full.
The point to watch is cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}.
Traffic: growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@FY2024}} and the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}).
Regulation: airport charges are temporarily adjusted by average inflation, a rule that ends at the end of 2026, so revenue per passenger depends on the tariff application that follows.
Litigation: disputes with the Maltese government and employee claims concerning Malta International Airport were outstanding at the balance sheet date, which the group considers unfounded.
